To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methylation status of cyto-sines in the promoter region (-226∼-101) of the APP gene changes with age.
some cytosine residues in the promoter region are methylated in human brain and that this methylation is reduced with age.
methylation of cytosines in the promoter region –226∼−100 of the APP gene was frequent in the brain of aged individuals and decreased with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the promoter region of APP in the regulation of APP gene transcription.
the role of methylation in the regulation of APP gene transcription.
the study of the role of the promoter in APP gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methylation status of cyto-sines in the −226∼−102 promoter region of the human APP gene changes with age and that this change may be involved in the regulation of the expression of the APP gene.
the methylation status of cyto-sines in the promoter region is not a determinant factor for the expression level of the APP gene.
the present findings suggest that some cytosine methylation in the APP gene may play a role in the development of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
demethylation of cytosine residues with age in the APP gene promoter region may be related to the pathogenesis of AD.
the methylation status in the promoter region may be a factor that determines the expression levels of APP in the human brain.

the methylation status of cyto-sines in the promoter region may be one of the factors determining the level of APP mRNA and protein expression in the brain and that its change with age may have significance for the development of AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we identified a novel promoter element in the APP gene and that the promoter element is demethylated with age.
the promoter of APP gene contains several CpG islands, which are frequently methylated.
we have identified the first DNA methylation site in a promoter region in a human gene that decreases with age.
